SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 975236
Permit API: 117-21807
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 11/08/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an ADMIN inspection of the Seneca Resources - Gee 848 on 11/8/22 in response to receipt of results from sample 4427-282.As noted in the previous inspection IR#3437521 dated 10/5/22, "three red tanks were observed baffled together in secondary containment. Fluid in red tank secondary containment had a field measured conductivity of 19.99mS/cm. Puddles and standing water were observed on the pad surface. The puddles along the southern end of the red tank secondary containment had a field measured conductivity of 19.2mS/cm. Moving due south away from the secondary containment the field conductivity of the puddles on the pad surface dropped to 14mS/cm and 12.4mS/cm at approximately 12 feet from the containment. The elevated field conductivity was also observed along the western edge of the red tank secondary containment. Sample 4427-282 was collected from the puddle along the southern end of secondary containment with a field measured conductivity of 19.2mS/cm."The attached sample results show elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides indicative of the presence of a regulated substance. Copies of the sample results will be provided to the operator via email. Violations of the following regulation are cited against the Gee 848 22H, API #117-21807:SWMA 30125 Pa Code 78a.56(a)CSL 402(b) is cited as CONTINUING

Comments: On 4/14/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Stoorza well site. This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a water puddle south of a pile of waste that was excavated from the Grippo well site. During an inspection on 3/21/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid was in a 3' x 12' x 0.5" water puddle on the unprotected pad surface. The puddle was adjacent to and on the south side of the northeast excavated material pile. The fluid field tested at over 20 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-048 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.642311 Long: -76.360168.On 4/12/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and chlorides released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 1 and 2.Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3524618 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

Comments: On 10/24/22 at 0929 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Wise Richard 4 well (API 065-25991) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. in response to notification that the production fluid tank had overflowed. The well is located in a fenced-in area of a pasture. The well is tagged and a site ID sign is posted. The valve on the well head is open and gas could be heard escaping the pressure release valve on the separator. It was observed that production fluid has overflowed from the tank onto the ground around the separator, tank, and meter housing. The fluid was contained to the fenced-in area and did not appear to exceed 1 barrel in volume. It was observed that the tank was still filled to capacity.Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and CSL 402(b) are being cited for this inspection for the release of production fluids onto the ground. These violations will be resolved upon remediation of the site and submission of associated disposal receipts to the Department.

Inspection Date: 7/16/2025
Comments: On July 16, 2025 DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. EQT acquired the Porter Well Pad from Olympus on 7/1/2025 (Transfer approved by the DEP on 7/14/2025), therefore EQT takes full responsibility of the incident addressed in IR 4004278, where violations were issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a produced water, freshwater and frack chemical mixture. Accompanying during today's inspection was EQT's Lance Barnes, Olympus's Kyle Borden and SPSI's Joe Perry.At the time of this inspection an Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance and in the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan. Operator information on the sign does not match the plans. The DEP recommends the Operator promptly update the plans as applicable. An access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During IR 4004278, the DEP screened the release area and collected elevated conductivity readings in an area that was scraped 2-4 inches deep as well as at the base/underneath an AST (inadvertently referred to as freshwater impoundment in IR 4004278) on site. At the time of that inspection, Olympus's Laura Karosic stated once fracking is complete (7/11-12/ 2024), the AST would be removed from the well site and further remediation efforts would be conducted in the release area.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the AST to be removed from the well site. The area where the AST was as well as the previously scraped release area all appeared to be newly scraped. A ditch was observed to be dug and bordering the secondary containment within the release area. The DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the newly scraped release area as well as the ditch. The DEP collected soil readings of 0.0171 mS, 0.0605 mS, and 0.026 mS in the newly scraped release area, and 2.33 mS in a puddle of cloudy fluid observed in the ditch. These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil reading taken on the well site perimeter (0.1247 mS). The readings collected in the scraped areas are comparable to the background reading, however readings collected in the ditch are elevated. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Barnes and Mr. Perry informed the DEP that the observed to be newly scraped release area is reportedly remediated, however the ditch and area underneath the containment is not. The DEP inquired why/how the area under the containment is contaminated when the release originated on top of the containment. Mr. Perry hypothesized that released fluids that were sitting on the graveled well pad/under the AST were washed underneath the secondary containment during heavy rainfall following the release. Once the rain ceased and the AST was removed, contaminated fluids leached out from under the containment in the release area, therefore the ditch is being utilized to catch and contain any of the leached contaminated fluid. Mr. Barnes and Mr. Borden stated that drilling will be completed in approx. 8-10 days, then the containment will be pulled and remediation efforts will be conducted in the remaining contaminated locations.The DEP recommends the EQT promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).During IR 4004278 the DEP requested the following:-The Operator submit a written response that includes an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released.-The Operator follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) -The Operator assess the impacts to the WOC from the release.-The Operator submit a NOV response by 7/23/25.--These have yet to be received as of 7/16/25Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued to EQT for the 1-3 barrel release and for failure to remove the contaminated fluid from the ground within 15 days of the pollution incident.

At approximately 11:00 the well was vented and the bubbling could no longer be heard. At approximately 11:36 the methane levels in the annulus dropped to 9% methane by volume. For safety reasons only one slam bar hole was placed in the ground on the windward side of the well bore due to the high amount of methane flowing from the annulus. 3% LEL was detected in this slam bar hole. At this time, the Department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/14/2022
Comments: On April 14, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. The soil in the area where the water from the seep had been pooling up has been excavated and removed. A small berm has been built in the area and a tarp has been dug in to collect stormwater. This area is being vacuumed as necessary. The DEP screened the pooled water on the downgradient side of the built berm and the conductivity was 365 uS/cm. An area to the south of the area impacted from the seep of the northwest stormwater vault that had been previously excavated to remove contaminated soil from the seep was screened for soil conductivity. The screening resulted in a measurement of 2.42 mS/cm in a small area. The area of high conductivity was shown to STL Resources Ken Shade. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/29/2025 to EQT ARO LLC in Cogan House Township, Lycoming county. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/29/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8215507
Permit API: 081-20563
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/29/2025
Comments: On January 29, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC H Lyle Landon Well Pad A. This inspection is a follow up to EQT reporting a spill on January 24, 2025, where a dump to one of the production fluid tanks failed. Upon failing, the pressure caused production fluid to mist outside of containment onto the well pad surface. According to EQT, it was thought that the majority of the production fluid was released into the production fluid containment. DEP placed a phone call to Rick Hall with EQT at 0848 on January 29, 2025 to gather more information on the spill. Mr. Hall informed DEP that during EQT's investigation of the spill that more than a mist event had occurred. While the majority of the produced fluid spilled into containment, an area of high soil conductivity was found outside of containment to the south next to the containment wall. EQT suspects there is an area of the liner for the containment that is leaking. Since January 24, 2025, EQT has vacuumed all the fluid out of the containment and power washed the containment liner. Mr. Hall said there were no visible or apparent holes found. The impacted soil that could be removed has been excavated. EQT plans to remove the production fluid tanks and the containment to investigate and remove the remainder of the impacted soil underneath the containment. A schedule for this process has not yet been made. EQT plans to monitor the area and remove impacted soil or production fluid as needed until the area can be completely remediated. On January 24, 2025, Penn E and R was onsite to collect waste classification samples and oversee the excavation. EQT plans to go through the Act 2 remediation process due to the unknown volume of fluid that leaked through the containment.Due to the spill of production fluid outside of containment violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

Comments: On January 3, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection on the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3435475 where violations were outstanding due to a missing Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plans, and no NOV response received from the operator. Also, no production reports had been submitted since 2014 per Department database, at the time of that inspection.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign was present at the well site entrance (see photo 1). No Emergency Response plans, or other required documents were onsite. No evidence of leaks or discharge could be found around the new production tanks, and they appeared to be sound at the time of inspection. However, they were not equipped with secondary containment (see photos 3 and 8). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the earthen berms surrounding these tanks, and at the bases of these tanks (see photos 4-7). The well tag and required operator's information was present on the meter box (see photo 8). The Additional piping and production equipment was left onsite. Some tire rutting was observed at the back of the well site looking from the road, which could be due to third party traversing (see photo 10). The ground overall was soft, which could lead to future stabilization concerns. Therefore, the Department recommends that the operator take additional stabilization measures to prevent any potential E and S issues from developing.Based on observations from today's inspection, the violations that were continued in IR 3435475 shall remain outstanding, since no changes were made since and no NOV response has been received to date. An additional violation shall be issued against the production tanks, since they are not equipped with secondary containment in an unconventional site.

Unconventional: No

Comments: On May 14, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4179087, 4179852, 4179896, and 4179921.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/26/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/26/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S Plan is present on site but has not been updated to depict streams and wetlands along the access road.- The entire length of the access road appears to have been graded, seeded, and mulched. - CFS remains improperly implemented or maintained at several points along the access road (Photos 3-8, 11-16, 19-21).- The outlet to Culvert 2 (Photo 12) and the inlet to Culvert 3 (Photo 13) remain blocked at this time.- Orange construction fence and CFS does not appear to have been installed along the access road where a wetland was identified by Department Biologists (Photo 22).- Sedimentation is observed at multiple points along the access road (Photos 6-7, 20-21).- Sedimentation at Culverts 5 and 8 appears to be threatening the stream, however no active discharge to the streams is observed at this time. - Regrading of the access road near the previous location of the production tank appears to have resulted in sediment being pushed to the end of the access road, which appears to be currently held by brush. No CFS is installed in this area. The Department recommends pulling the sediment back and installing CFS to prevent sedimentation off of the access road.- The well site appears to be seeded and mulched at this time.Violations remain outstanding for erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, failure to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, failure to identify wetlands and streams in the E and S plan, failure to maintain culverts on the access road, and failure to implement/maintain E and S BMPs.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 8/05/2024
Comments: On August 5 2024, the Department responded to an incident occuring in Fayette County, Washington Township. On August 5 2024 at 11:25am, the Department received a report that around 11:00am a truck on loading produced water from the production tanks had equipment malfunction resulting in an estimate of over 5 gallons spilling onto the ground. An EQT representative stated that it spilled on the ground but did not get into the waterways of commonwealth. At the time of this inspection, Act 9 Sign was present but faded. The Department recommends that the Operator update the Act 9 Sign as appropriate to ensure compliance with 78a55. At the time of this inspection, a third party representative of EQT (Specialized Professional Services Inc.) was completing clean up of the affected area. Equipment was present. Excavation was actively occurring during this inspection. The affected area was near the off loading and on/off loading area of the production tanks. According to a SPSI representative, a truck was unloading production fluid from the production tanks and had a failure at the connection, which caused production fluid to spill near the on/off loading site and visually extended down the side of the access road roughly 50ft. The SPSI representative stated that roughly 10 to 15 gallons spilled. Soil conductivity readings as well as a background soil conductivity reading was taken. The background soil conductivity reading was 0.1145mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken within the affected area were 0.458mS, 0.0031mS, and 0.0979mS. One reading in the visually affected area was elevated above the background reading of 0.1145mS. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the fluid release in accordance with 78a.66. The Department also requests the Operator evaluate the release that has occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred, to be provided in the requested NOV Response. The Department also requests waste manifests upon proper disposal of wastes generated from the spill remediation.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued at this time.
